{"issues":[{"number":5,"title":"Add a border filter that draws a solid band around the picture","body":"## What happens today

A URL that asks for `filters:border(12,red)` returns the picture unchanged. The server answers 200. No band is drawn. Nothing in the response says the name was ignored.

## What should happen

`border(width, color)` adds a solid band of `width` pixels on all four sides of the picture. The picture keeps its own pixels. The output grows by twice the width in each dimension. The band is added after the crop and the resize, so the band is never scaled. `color` is a color name such as `red` or a hex value such as `ff0000`. `border(0,red)` leaves the picture alone. A transparent picture keeps its transparent inside and only the band is painted. The filter works together with the other filters in the same URL, in the order they are written.

## How to see it

Start the course server. Open this path against it:

`/unsafe/240x180/filters:border(12,red)/hills.png`

Today the browser shows the hills picture at 240 by 180 with no band. When the filter works, the browser shows the same picture inside a 12 pixel red band, 264 by 204.

## Where it came from

This one is the course's own request. thumbor has no border filter and nobody has asked for one upstream, so there is no conversation to read.","state":"OPEN","user":{"login":"DylanPant"},"labels":["menu"],"assignees":[],"created_at":"2026-11-10T23:22:51Z","updated_at":"2026-11-10T23:22:51Z"},{"number":4,"title":"Resizing a transparent image to a very wide, very short size returns an empty picture","body":"## What happens today

Ask the image server for a picture at an aspect ratio far from the source's, and the result is empty or an error. A square transparent PNG requested at 800x20 comes back as an 800x20 image in which every pixel is fully transparent. The browser shows nothing where the picture should be. A very wide source asked to fit in a 1x1 box, or asked for a width only, returns a 500 error page instead of an image.

## What should happen

Every request for a size of at least one pixel per side returns a real picture of that size. The 800x20 request should show the colored bars of the source stretched into a wide strip. The fit-in requests should return a 1x1 image and a 100x1 image.

## How to see it

Start the image server and open this path on it:

    /unsafe/800x20/rainbow.png

The source is a 16x16 transparent PNG with vertical rainbow bars. Today the page shows a blank 800x20 image. After the fix the page shows a rainbow strip 800 pixels wide and 20 pixels tall.

Also open:

    /unsafe/fit-in/1x1/940x2.png

Today it shows a 500 error page. After the fix it shows a 1x1 image.

And this one, a width only:

    /unsafe/fit-in/100x0/940x2.png

Today it shows a 500 error page. After the fix it shows a 100x1 image.

## Where it came from

This is a real bug, reported on the thumbor project as thumbor/thumbor#1711 (https://github.com/thumbor/thumbor/issues/1711). Some GIF files use a palette and mark one palette entry as transparent. The sticker image in the course images folder is one of them. Its background is transparent, so the page shows through around the blue disc.

Ask the image server for that GIF at a new size. The GIF that comes back is fully opaque. The area that used to be transparent is now a solid black box around the sticker.

The same request with PNG output keeps the transparency. The problem needs a palette source, GIF output, and the PILLOW_PRESERVE_INDEXED_MODE setting on. That setting is on by default.

## What should happen

A resize must not change which pixels are transparent. The GIF that comes back carries a transparency index. The pixels that were transparent in the source are transparent in the output. A GIF with no transparency stays opaque. PNG output keeps its partial alpha.

## How to see it

Start the image server with the course configuration. Open this path in the browser:

/unsafe/240x160/sticker.gif

Today you see the sticker inside a solid black box. After the fix the box is gone and the browser's own background shows around the sticker. The Pillow engine handles this request, not gifsicle.

## Where it came from

This is a real bug, reported on the thumbor project as thumbor/thumbor#1886 (https://github.com/thumbor/thumbor/issues/1886). round_corner with the transparent flag set, written out as PNG or WebP, draws a thin dark outline along every curved corner. The pixels on the curve stay fully opaque and have their colors scaled toward black. Over any page background the corner looks as if it were traced with a dark pencil. The opaque form of the filter, without the transparent flag, blends its edge cleanly into the fill color.

## What should happen

The curve is smoothed through the alpha channel. Pixels on the edge keep their original color and become partly transparent, so the picture fades into whatever is behind it with no outline. Output formats without alpha, such as JPEG, should still show the fill color in the corners.

## How to see it

Start the image server and open this path in the browser:

/unsafe/300x200/filters:round_corner(60,255,255,255,1):format(png)/example.jpg

Zoom into any corner of the picture. Today a dark ring follows the arc where the picture meets the background. After the fix the arc fades into the background with no ring. The same path with format(webp) in place of format(png) shows the same ring. The image file is example.jpg.

## Where it came from

This is a real bug, reported on the thumbor project as thumbor/thumbor#1687 (https://github.com/thumbor/thumbor/issues/1687). Ask for a small image inside a larger fit-in box, with a fill color and no_upscale. The server returns the source image at its own size. There is no colored canvas around it. An 80 by 50 source requested at 300 by 300 comes back as 80 by 50. The order of the two filters does not change the result.

## What should happen

no_upscale limits only the picture. It must not shrink the canvas. The response is 300 by 300. The fill color covers the canvas. The source sits in the middle at its own size. Both filter orders give the same picture. This holds in plain resize mode, fit-in mode and full-fit-in mode. An adaptive fit-in request still picks its orientation from the size the client asked for. A no_upscale request that uses orig as a dimension returns the image instead of an error.

## How to see it

Start the course server. Open this path in the browser:

/unsafe/fit-in/300x300/filters:fill(red):no_upscale():format(png)/small.png

small.png is an 80 by 50 blue rectangle. Today the browser shows only that blue rectangle. After the fix the browser shows a 300 by 300 red square with the blue rectangle centered inside it.

## Where it came from

This is a real bug, reported on the thumbor project as thumbor/thumbor#1883 (https://github.com/thumbor/thumbor/issues/1883).         # fades into the background with no dark ring. Today those pixels are

        # issue reports.

    "body": "We run thumbor in production and this bug affects one of our users, so we dug deeper into the root cause — and it turns out it's **not a transparency bug**, which means #1774 won't fix it.

**Root cause:** in `thumbor/transformer.py`, `auto_crop()` computes

```python
crop_height = int(round(source_width * self.target_height / target_width, 0))
```

For a 1x1 source resized to 50x25 this gives `round(0.5) = 0` (Python banker's rounding), so the image is cropped to `(0, 0, 1, 0)` — an empty 1x0 image. Any target ratio ≥ 2:1 on a 1x1 source triggers it.

**Why #1774 doesn't help (and actually makes it worse):** the patched `resize()` calls `has_transparency()`, which does `min(self.image.convert("RGBA").getchannel("A").getextrema())`. Reproduced on the `pr-1774` branch with Pillow 11.3.0.

```python
crop_width = max(1, crop_width)
crop_height = max(1, crop_height)
```

# thumbor imaging service

"""Regression test for issue #3: a resized GIF must keep its transparent
background.

Some GIF files use a palette and mark one palette entry as transparent. After
a resize, the Pillow engine quantizes the RGBA image back to P for GIF output;
the palette still carries the alpha, but Pillow does not set
image.info["transparency"], so the GIF writer drops the transparent index and
the background becomes a solid opaque block.
"""

from io import BytesIO

from PIL import Image, ImageDraw

from thumbor.config import Config
from thumbor.context import Context
from thumbor.engines.pil import Engine

WIDTH = 240
HEIGHT = 160
RED = (255, 0, 0)
TRANSPARENT_INDEX = 255


def make_transparent_gif():
    """A palette GIF whose background is a single transparent index."""
    image = Image.new("P", (WIDTH, HEIGHT), 0)
    palette = [0, 0, 0] * 256
    palette[0:3] = list(RED)
    palette[TRANSPARENT_INDEX * 3 : TRANSPARENT_INDEX * 3 + 3] = [0, 0, 0]
    image.putpalette(palette)

    draw = ImageDraw.Draw(image)
    # a red disc in the middle; everything else keeps the transparent index
    for y in range(HEIGHT):
        for x in range(WIDTH):
            dx = x - WIDTH / 2
            dy = y - HEIGHT / 2
            if dx * dx + dy * dy <= 60 * 60:
                image.putpixel((x, y), 0)

    del draw

    buffer = BytesIO()
    image.save(buffer, format="GIF", transparency=TRANSPARENT_INDEX)
    return buffer.getvalue()


def get_context():
    cfg = Config(
        SECURITY_KEY="ACME-SEC",
        ENGINE="thumbor.engines.pil",
        PILLOW_PRESERVE_INDEXED_MODE=True,
    )
    cfg.LOADER = "thumbor.loaders.file_loader"
    cfg.STORAGE = "thumbor.storages.no_storage"
    return Context(config=cfg)


def count_transparent_pixels(image):
    alpha = image.convert("RGBA").getchannel("A")
    return sum(1 for value in alpha.getdata() if value == 0)


def test_resized_gif_keeps_transparency():
    source_bytes = make_transparent_gif()

    source = Image.open(BytesIO(source_bytes))
    assert source.mode == "P"
    assert count_transparent_pixels(source) > 0

    engine = Engine(get_context())
    engine.extension = ".gif"
    engine.load(source_bytes, ".gif")
    engine.resize(WIDTH // 2, HEIGHT // 2)

    result_bytes = engine.read()

    result = Image.open(BytesIO(result_bytes))
    assert result.format == "GIF"
    assert "transparency" in result.info, (
        "resized GIF lost its transparency index; the background became opaque"
    )
    assert count_transparent_pixels(result) > 0
